theory.say:
• Lien: a bill with a legal right to payment from the settlement before the client's share
• John Doe's $40,000: two liens asserted, five checked and found absent, each sourced; not his until all are found, sorted, resolved in writing
• Legal basis decides how far a lien bends: sort one wrong and you overpay or freeze the payout
• Top: providers on an LOP, a Letter of Protection promising payment from the settlement; very negotiable
• Next: health insurance subrogation; made whole means repaid only once the client is fully compensated, common fund that the lienholder shares recovery costs
• Lower: Medicare and Medicaid, strict formulas; bottom: ERISA self-funded employer plans, hardest to reduce

frame.say:
• Providers on an LOP sit high: they often reduce to get paid now
• Private health insurance sits moderate, subject to made whole or common fund
• Medicare and Medicaid sit low; ERISA self-funded plans very low, under federal law
• Riverton Spine & Rehab is the LOP provider, top of the ladder; Peach State is fully insured, not ERISA
• Fully insured: the employer bought a policy, so state law generally governs reduction; Atty. Thorne confirms
• Triple-check each lien: timeliness, Peach State's 02/27/2026 notice; perfection, Riverton has an LOP only, no recorded or served notice; scope, strike lines outside the collision

• Every claimant, absent ones too: "none" with where and when you checked; prior attorney: "none known to John Doe"
• Two asserted: Peach State and Riverton; PIP has no reimbursement right; Crescent can't balance-bill; Health Plan: plan documents, funding status escalated, fully insured on file

theory.say:
• BI stream alone: $6,179.92 against $7,965.00 in liens, John Doe takes home nothing; he actually nets $20,359.92
• Net Sheet: one page, every dollar in and out: $40,000 from three carriers in two streams, out as five checks
• A dollar that can't be traced on the sheet doesn't leave trust
• Stream 1, third-party BI: the at-fault driver's insurer; usually exhausted to its limit first as a legal step
• Stream 2, first-party UM: the client's or a resident relative's policy; opens once BI is used up or the driver is uninsured
• Double-dipping: the same dollar counted twice; trace each dollar's source so liens are paid right; the total shows both streams
